subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity sizing & latency SLOs for Finrise
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finrise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity sizing & latency SLOs for Finrise

Hi Olivia / Finrise team — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps to get Dedicated capacity validated for your latency and throughput SLOs.

Recap / requirements you called out:
- Target 99th-pct latency: <= 350 ms for streaming token chunks (model responds via streaming).
- Sustained throughput: ~300 requests/sec (mixed prompt lengths; average input ~1.2k tokens, average generation ~60 tokens).
- Peak concurrency: ~60 concurrent requests.
- Streaming chunk size: prefer ~64-token chunks with sub-100ms inter-chunk latency for UI UX.
- Model: you indicated an internal fork of Llama-2-70B (quantized to int8), and one lighter variant for lower-cost fallbacks.
- Data residency: US only; SOC2 requirements discussed (we'll surface audit artifacts).

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the breakdown of traffic (percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests) and expected growth over next 3 months?
2) Please share any existing benchmark CSVs if you have them (we can run them through our harness).

What we'll do next:
- Attach: initial sizing recommendation & benchmark summary (redwood_dedicated_sizing_v1.pdf, benchmark_summary.csv). This is preliminary; we'll iterate after we get your real benchmark artifacts.
- Proposal: schedule a 60–90 minute technical validation session (we'll run your sample workload through our Dedicated cluster and measure tail latencies and sustained throughput).
- Suggested sequencing: 1) quick validation session; 2) prototype Dedicated reservation (1–2 weeks); 3) production reservation + SLA.

Provisional sizing notes in the attachment (high-level):
- H100 (80GB) nodes: best tail latency for 70B quantized models; lower headroom needed vs A100; recommended for strict 99th-pct <=350ms.
- A100 (40GB) nodes: viable with more instances; cost-effective for fallback variant and for batched workloads.
- L40/RTX-class: good for dev/preview, not recommended for production 70B SLOs.
- Reserved throughput: we typically size by reserved tokens/sec and concurrency groups. For your numbers we estimate needing equivalent of ~6–8 H100 slots (depending on KV cache hit rate / prompt reuse).

Suggested next steps:
- Olivia: confirm traffic split & share benchmark file (if available).
- Let us know 2x 1‑hour windows this week for a tech validation.

Thanks — I'll loop in Marissa and Rafael to run the session and capture the test plan.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@finrise.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity sizing & latency SLOs for Finrise

Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few details and attaching our latest internal benchmark workbook (finrise_current_benchmarks.xlsx).

Answers / clarifications:
- Traffic split: ~85% streaming (UI tokens), 15% non-streaming (batch generation).
- Growth: expect 20% month-over-month for next quarter from current pilot.
- Model: core is an internal Llama-2-70B-int8 fork; we also plan an Open-Llama-13B-int8 fallback for cost-sensitive routes.
- Typical prompts: median prompt 900 tokens; median generation 45 tokens.
- SLOs: the 99th <= 350ms is firm for our paid tier; best-effort for free tier.
- Compliance: SOC2 in scope; will want KMS integration and audit logs.

Constraints / questions from our side:
- Do you have publicized per-GPU 99th-pct numbers for Llama-2-70B-int8 on H100 vs A100 for streaming workloads?
- How does Redwood reserve throughput across concurrency groups (do you carve per-GPU slots or provision per-request concurrency)?

We can do a validation session next week — Tue 7/21 10:00–11:30am ET or Wed 7/22 2:00–3:30pm ET. Please confirm which works.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | Finrise
olivia@finrise.com

Attachment: finrise_current_benchmarks.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finrise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity sizing & latency SLOs for Finrise

Hi Olivia — great, thanks for the workbook. Confirming Wed 7/22 2:00–3:30pm ET works for our team (we'll book the 90-minute slot to include a short walkthrough + live validation).

Answers to your questions and a clearer sizing sketch (high level):
- Publicized numbers: we don't publish a one-size-fits-all 99th-pct table because tail latency changes with prompt length distribution, KV cache reuse, and streaming chunk size — but our in-house benchmarks (attached summary) show for Llama-2-70B-int8:
  - H100 (80GB): 99th-pct streaming chunk latency ~220–360 ms (depends on chunk size & KV cache hit).
  - A100 (40GB): 99th-pct streaming chunk latency ~320–520 ms (more variance at tail).
  - L40/RTX: typically >500 ms at tail for 70B streams — not recommended for paid-tier SLO.

- Reservation model: Dedicated reservations are expressed as reserved throughput units and concurrency groups. Practically we map that to a fixed number of GPU slots (e.g., H100 slots) that are kept available for your routes. For example, to meet 300 req/s sustained with 60 concurrent streaming sessions, we recommend reserving throughput equivalent to 6 H100 slots (conservative) — that assumes 70% KV cache hit and typical prompt lengths you shared. If cache hit is low we may bump to 8 slots.

- Streaming behavior: we recommend 64-token chunking and enabling low-latency kernel paths in our runtime. We'll instrument inter-chunk latency during the validation to ensure ~<100ms between chunks for your UI.

- Recommended starting reservation: 6x H100 (80GB) nodes, reserve throughput for 350k tokens/min sustained (we'll detail in the sizing PDF). Fallback: 10x A100 (40GB) nodes if you prefer more smaller instances for cost predictability.

Next steps for the validation session (Wed 7/22 2pm ET):
- We'll run your attached benchmark harness through our Dedicated test cluster. Please provide 1–2 anonymized example prompts and a short list of user IDs to simulate concurrency.
- We'll capture: 50/90/99/99.9 tail latencies for both streaming chunk and full-response completion, throughput stability over 10-minute sustained run, and resource utilization per GPU.
- Outcome: updated sizing doc, recommended reservation, and a short follow-up with PO/contractual options if results look good.

Attached: updated sizing PDF + summarized CSV (redwood_dedicated_sizing_v1.pdf, benchmark_summary.csv).

I'll book the calendar and share the validation run checklist. Marissa / Rafael will lead the run — Marissa will bring the harness; Rafael will observe infra-level metrics and collect traces.

Best,
Aditya
